intelligence.essence: Atomic Scope Evolution Law: NayaNET shall treat taxonomy revisions, evidence withdrawals, qualification changes, baseline promotions and consequential authorizations as operations over one canonically ordered governance state. Every change must be independently qualified within its scope, revalidated at its authoritative commit boundary, and recorded with reconstructable provenance. Stale or ambiguous state shall not create qualification or execution authority. Unaffected independently supported capabilities shall be preserved. The desired behavior: 'A scope is being split while a provider regression is being investigated and a model promotion is pending. I can prepare all three changes concurrently. But before any becomes authoritative, I will determine the canonical order, reject stale assumptions, preserve unaffected proof, and ensure ACT cannot rely on a qualification that no longer applies.' That is how NayaNET evolves its intelligence continuously without letting concurrent evolution corrupt its understanding of what is true, current, or authorized.
intelligence.falsifier: A merge committing on a pre-withdrawal incident revision; a promotion silently reinterpreting an old scope across new split children; an ACT authorization on a cached classification that a taxonomy change just invalidated; a rollback that resurrects a cached certificate via a reused version number; an ambiguous historical record silently allocated to a convenient child; a remote in-flight effect claimed as prevented by a local withdrawal; a 'verified' incident that was only ever an alert flag workers could ignore.

human_view.meaning: Every part of the system can be right on its own and still combine into something dangerous. One worker promotes a shared baseline while another discovers a regression in one of its member scopes; the authorizer approves a retry using a scope that was just split and no longer carries the qualification. The law: nothing — no merge, no split, no new scope, no promotion, no consequential authorization — may commit using stale evidence. Every decision must be valid against one authoritative, internally consistent snapshot of the world. Three different jobs stay separate: the taxonomy says what belongs together, qualification says what has been proven, and LAW says what may be done — none may silently grant authority through another. The commit sequence is prepare, verify independently, check LAW, then one atomic moment where the system locks, re-reads everything, and either publishes or rejects as stale. Three races are worked through in both orders: withdrawal-vs-merge, split-vs-promotion, new-scope-vs-authorization — each with the exact required outcome for each order, including the honest limitation that no database can revoke a remote effect already in flight (it must be preserved, reconciled, and claimed only as far as the real enforcement boundary reaches). Incidents get a fast containment path — withdraw reliance now, rebuild models later — as a governed write, never a flaggable alert. History is never rewritten: splits preserve the parent, ambiguous records stay ambiguous, and a rollback is a new revision, never a reused number. Twelve concurrency tests prove it, including crash-between-commit-and-index-refresh, phantom inserts, and the ABA resurrection. And performance is protected honestly: everything can run concurrently except the final authoritative conflict decision — serialize the verdict, not the work.

Permanent contributions: the one-governance-state principle (taxonomy/qualification/LAW separation), the monotonic governance epoch with never-reused versions, the PREPARE→VERIFY→LAW→ATOMIC COMMIT→PROPAGATE boundary, the three worked races with both-order invariants (W≺M / M≺W), the Authorize(a,s) five-conjunct predicate with the LAW/ACT two-boundary split, the fenced-execution-intent pattern (never hold a transaction across a provider call), the fast containment path as a governed write, the no-rewrite history discipline with ABA-proof rollbacks, the R1–R12 harness with its four invariants plus historical integrity, and the serialize-the-verdict-not-the-work performance principle. Shawn's scoping stands: isolated harness first.

Revalidate at the commit boundary; reject stale verification. Keep taxonomy, qualification, and LAW as separate authorities. Work all three races in both commit orders. Give incidents a fast governed containment path. Never rewrite history; never reuse versions.
